Your job is to address issue #3382.
First, read the file __issue_context__.json in the current working directory to get the issue title, body, and comments.

IMPORTANT: You are working in a local copy of ai4curation/eval-ont-agent-cl.
The issue context was imported from obophenotype/cell-ontology for evaluation purposes.
Do NOT attempt to clone, checkout, or interact with any remote repositories.
Stay in the current working directory and make all changes here.

On completion, commit your changes locally. Do NOT push - that will be handled automatically.
Don't commit files you did not edit.

After committing, create two files:

1. ISSUE_COMMENTS.md: Updates on the issue regarding its status. This will be fed back to the originating issue.
2. PR_COMMENTS.md: A description of your changes, and the rationale. This will be fed back to the originating PR.

I will take care of feeding these back to the GitHub repo, you just need to create them. Don't commit them,
and don't attempt to interact with the github repo.

If the original issue is not clear, ask for clarification in ISSUE_COMMENTS.md, and do not
commit any changes. The PR_COMMENTS.md can be empty in this case.

Your PR_COMMENTS.md should be a human-readable description of your changes, and the rationale. Include any checklists
you created for yourself and completed. If you performed validation, background research, etc, be sure to mention this.

Your ISSUE_COMMENTS.md need not replicate what is in PR_COMMENTS.md, and in many cases can be terse but polite, e.g
"changes committed in PR #<NN>" (note: use the literal `<NN>` in the output, I will replace it with the actual PR number).

If the issue is a complex one, you can create a high level summary of the decisions you made. If things are not clear
or if you want particular people in the thread to check particular aspects you can mention them.

Follow any CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md or other relevant files in the repository.

{
  "body": "**CL term**
[CL_0001041](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CL_0001041) — CD8-positive, CXCR3-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell  

**Suggested revision of class hierarchy**
Change the property for C-X-C chemokine receptor type 3 from `has part` to `has plasma membrane part` ([RO_0002104](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002104)).  

**Rationale**  
Currently, the C-X-C chemokine receptor type 3 of CL_0001041 is described with the `has part` property. We suggest changing this to `has plasma membrane part`, which more accurately reflects the localization of CXCR3.  

For example, the following CXCR3-labeled terms are described with `lacks_plasma_membrane_part`:  
- [CL_0001051](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CL_0001051) — CD4-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative, alpha-beta T cell  
[CL_0001052](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CL_0001052) — CD8-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative, alpha-beta T cell 

**Additional Note**
Upon examining other CL terms, it appears that the following PR terms are described not only with “has (or lacks) plasma membrane part” but also with “has part” or “lacks part.” It is unclear whether this distinction is made intentionally.:
immunoglobulin iota chain (PR_000001858)
immunoglobulin lambda-like polypeptide 1 (PR_000001859)
protein c-Fos (PR_000007597)
myeloperoxidase (PR_000010543)
transcription factor PU.1 (PR_000001944)
V(D)J recombination-activating protein 1 (PR_000003457)
V(D)J recombination-activating protein 2 (PR_000003460)

Thank you for your consideration.
",
  "comments": [],
  "title": "[Class hierarchy] Change CXCR3 property in CD8+ CXCR3+ alpha-beta regulatory T cell",
  "url": "https://github.com/obophenotype/cell-ontology/issues/3382"
}

## Summary

Addresses issue #3382 by updating the logical definition of `CL_0001041` (`CD8-positive, CXCR3-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell`). The CXCR3 (`PR_000001207`) restriction now uses `has plasma membrane part` (`RO_0002104`) instead of the broader `has part` (`BFO_0000051`).

## Rationale

CXCR3 is a cell-surface chemokine receptor, so modeling it as a plasma membrane part is more specific and consistent with related CXCR3-positive and CXCR3-negative classes in CL, including the negative CXCR3 terms cited in the issue.

## Checklist

- [x] Reviewed issue context from `__issue_context__.json`.
- [x] Checked existing axioms for `CL_0001041` and CXCR3 (`PR_000001207`) in `src/ontology/cl-edit.owl`.
- [x] Updated only `src/ontology/cl-edit.owl`.
- [x] Confirmed the updated `CL_0001041` axiom uses `RO_0002104`.
- [x] Validated OWL functional syntax with `robot convert --input src/ontology/cl-edit.owl --output /tmp/cl-edit.ofn`.

Signed-off-by: GitHub Cop

{
  "body": "**CL term**
[CL_0001041](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CL_0001041) — CD8-positive, CXCR3-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell  

**Suggested revision of class hierarchy**
Change the property for C-X-C chemokine receptor type 3 from `has part` to `has plasma membrane part` ([RO_0002104](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002104)).  

**Rationale**  
Currently, the C-X-C chemokine receptor type 3 of CL_0001041 is described with the `has part` property. We suggest changing this to `has plasma membrane part`, which more accurately reflects the localization of CXCR3.  

For example, the following CXCR3-labeled terms are described with `lacks_plasma_membrane_part`:  
- [CL_0001051](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CL_0001051) — CD4-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative, alpha-beta T cell  
[CL_0001052](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CL_0001052) — CD8-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative, alpha-beta T cell 

**Additional Note**
Upon examining other CL terms, it appears that the following PR terms are described not only with “has (or lacks) plasma membrane part” but also with “has part” or “lacks part.” It is unclear whether this distinction is made intentionally.:
immunoglobulin iota chain (PR_000001858)
immunoglobulin lambda-like polypeptide 1 (PR_000001859)
protein c-Fos (PR_000007597)
myeloperoxidase (PR_000010543)
transcription factor PU.1 (PR_000001944)
V(D)J recombination-activating protein 1 (PR_000003457)
V(D)J recombination-activating protein 2 (PR_000003460)

Thank you for your consideration.
",
  "comments": [],
  "title": "[Class hierarchy] Change CXCR3 property in CD8+ CXCR3+ alpha-beta regulatory T cell",
  "url": "https://github.com/obophenotype/cell-ontology/issues/3382"
}

## Summary

Addresses issue #3382 by updating the logical definition of `CL_0001041` (`CD8-positive, CXCR3-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell`). The CXCR3 (`PR_000001207`) restriction now uses `has plasma membrane part` (`RO_0002104`) instead of the broader `has part` (`BFO_0000051`).

## Rationale

CXCR3 is a cell-surface chemokine receptor, so modeling it as a plasma membrane part is more specific and consistent with related CXCR3-positive and CXCR3-negative classes in CL, including the negative CXCR3 terms cited in the issue.

- [x] Reviewed issue context from `__issue_context__.json`.
